widgets_values: The CLIP DOES NOT pass the character, image, generation, or any other information between the image and video models. In other words, one AI DOES NOT know what the other AI is doing, without your instructions. It helps both models to keep your image sizes/resolutions and prompts coherent or related. For example, in generating "Mito Ikumi" I had to prompt Wan with "A woman with blue eyes and short blonde hair" as I was receiving morphs in her hair and eye color. widgets_values:
This sets the latent pixels from Wai-Illustrious, and converts them into a form readable by Wan 2.2 using the Wai VAE. It then passes the image either directly to Wan or to a resizer and keyframer loop I made! 

If you are working in higher resolutions, you likely do not need to resize the image! 

If you are doing 480p ANIME gens, I would recommend enabling the resizer, as the Wan VAE can cause pixelation and jarred lines at lower sizes with anime gens, based on my experience and testing.

The resizer and keyframer are bypassed by default!

Also, you could drag the LIGHT BLUE IMAGE WIRE to the "start_image" input on the WAN vae and still use the resizer and Keyframer! The workflow can save a keyframe for you to be able to animate later! To check or save the 720p/480p frame, you can activate the "Keyframer" node with "Ctrl+B". Turn it off once you got it set so it won't auto save every time you regen from your locked source image! Do the reverse, dragging from the Resizer node to the Wan node to re-loop the resizer!

Lanczos is generally recommened "method" by the community for resizing! I stand by that, with honorable mentions for Area!

Default Tiled VAE Decode settings are 512 tile size, 64 overlap, 64 temporal size, and 8 temporal overlap.

The preferred sizes are 480x480 and 720x720. IF YOU run it, YOU have to set the RESOLUTION in BOTH the resize and Wan nodes!

TLDR: {Use up to 3 curly bracket strings|like this|to make cooler prompts|the AI chooses between all these options|sometimes it mixes things up though!}

ComfyUI has the function to create variance in a prompt using curly brackets "{" and "}" as well as a vertical bar separator "|" between items in the dynamic prompt creation. Here's an example "{red hair,short hair,curly hair|blonde hair,bob cut hair,straight hair|black hair,long hair,parted bangs}". During testing, I noticed that this is most predicable in image generation, though it can be used in video generation as well. The variance added is NOT stable, with more than 2 - 3 of these dynamic prompt strings, the model can generate very chaotic or uncanny valley, like scary smiles or extra limbs. This was most noticeable during video generation with bodily morphing. I recommend limiting your dynamic strings to below 3. I have not tested dynamic character strings such as {katsuragi misato|ayanami rei|ikari shinji}. Good luck, if that is your intent!

♡Additional Notes♡

♡ The Image and Video LoRA and Gen settings are pretty locked in! If you want to adjust anything outside your prompts! This thing is specially tuned to anime and hentai.

♡ This set up works with all kinds of resolutions! Check the notes above the Wan 2.2 workflow for precise setting recommendations! The default 4 step with 720x720 is a good starting place!

♡ I fixed as many generation settings as possible based on extensive generation and testing! These settings produced the best results on my system/set-up! Randomize for adventure, experimentation, and at your own risk!

♡ I use the FP8 distillation or the Q5 GGUFs for Wan 2.2 and other models derived from it, as my testing has shown a slight but noticeable improvement, with no more than a 10 percent increase in gen time.If that's "inconceivable", then try the Q4! I've tried the Q4_KS and Q4_KM, but I honestly don't know which Q4 is better, so they're both worth trying! I've heard the Q6 can be run on most commercial RTX GPUs as well! 

♡ You can also run SmoothMix's excellent GGUF, but BYPASS OR REMOVE THE LIGHTNING LORAS! SmoothMix already includes them! I would be careful about running too many custom mods and LoRAs, unless you're a master at ComfyUI. The balance can be tricky, and you need to be comfortable doing a LOT of generations, and I mean a LOT.

♡ I use 97 frames, 16 fps, and 6 steps with CFG of 1.1 for video gens. This makes a big difference! I've tested between 4-6 steps for the lightning LoRAs, and prefer 6 steps. I like to push the upper limits on purpose for the video quality.
The CFG is just enough to activate the negative prompt, which is mostly the default Wan prompt. I hate the eternal talking heads, so I added "talking" and "photorealistic" to reduce the Wan 2.2 base realism training. I've also added in some tuning to help with the hand off between high and low noise passes! This results in a clean 6 second video, which is easy for animation gen, gooning, posting, sound synch, and editing!

♡ Wan 2.2 default settings are 81 frames, 16 fps, 4 steps with lightning LoRA, CFG = 1.0 with lightning LoRA. If you want to run default settings, make sure to change the "start_at_step" and "end_at_step" values on the KSampler (Advanced) nodes! For high pass, it would be start: 0, end: 2. For low pass it would be start: 2, end: 999.

♡ For 720x720, my gen times are generally between 800-1000 seconds. For 480x480, it's about 300-500! It's significantly faster, BUT highly degrades the quality of output and motion, in my opinion from my experience and testing. Read the LoRA descriptions; most times LoRA strength works best between .6-.8! Try a low weight first, before experimenting and cranking things up!

♡ I reccomend SmoothMix's XXX Animations and tagging the "SmoothMixAnime" or "SmoothMixRealism" tags! Their Q_4 Wan 2.2 GGUF is EXCELLENT and COMPLETELY uncensored, and I'm testing the combination of the two with this setup! Use the "SmoothMixRealism" tag and alter the prompts if you want to lean into photorealism!

♡ For Prompting, I prefer a descriptive, cinematic, and motion-based approach! Less is often more with Wai and Wan!
Describe what you want to see in Wai Illustrious using the left most prompt boxes, and then describe what you want the subjects and scene to do in Wan 2.2 on the right hand side!
You don't really need to describe what things look like to Wan most times, but a bit of description for blurry or weird details (especially character traits like hair or eyes) can help the model stay on track during gens! If you want your Miku-chan to keep her aqua hair and eyes, you gotta tell Wan, or it might get "creative"!
